title: Randomize the sharer's attributes, with a behavioural share
why: Fixes the design cause: randomizing attributes in vignettes turns the descriptive close-tie and high-trust contrasts into causal estimates and removes bundling with the real contact.

power_target.basis: H2 close tie 0.030 vs MDE 0.0258; H5 high trust 0.057 vs MDE 0.051

rationale: In the source study close ties (+3.0 points, CI [1.0, 5.0]) and high trust (+5.7 points, CI [2.3, 9.1]) were associated with more sharing, but these attributes were respondents' ratings of real contacts and so bundle correlated traits. Randomizing tie and trust in a forwarded-post vignette tests whether they cause sharing of false headlines (misinformation was shared 18.2 points less than true headlines).
contribution: Turns descriptive tie-strength and trust contrasts into causal estimates, using a behavioural share outcome and a real-contact benchmark.
hypothesis: H1: a randomized close tie raises the probability of sharing by about 0.03. H2: randomized high trust raises it by about 0.05. Both effects hold for false headlines.
primary_outcome: Share of the forwarded post to the mock feed (binary).
comparison: Close vs distant tie and high vs low trust, within headline type. Standard errors are clustered by respondent. Headline type is a between-subject factor.
unresolved: The platform's randomization of tie and trust within each arm, the mock feed implementation, compensation and IRB number must be supplied by the research team.
label: Design advance

media: post_true: image stimulus to supply (a social media post showing a true, neutral news headline on a topic such as a c)
post_mis: image stimulus to supply (a social media post showing a false news headline on a disputed topic)
title: Does the misinformation penalty hold across belief in disputed claims?
why: Fixes the missing_moderator cause: it pre-selects the moderator from S3 and S8 and tests it with enough power instead of relying on a tertile contrast.

power_target.basis: S3 misinformation difference 0.056 (SE 0.017); interaction MDE is larger than main-effect MDE 0.031

rationale: The source found misinformation shared 18.2 points less than true/neutral content (95% CI [-20.4,-16.0]), but respondents with higher belief in disputed claims shared misinformation 5.6 points more (p<0.001), a tertile contrast that was underpowered and US-English only. This design pre-selects belief in disputed claims as the moderator, stratifies on it and on survey language (English/Spanish), and tests one registered interaction.
contribution: Tests whether the misinformation sharing penalty shrinks among high-belief respondents and whether it generalizes to Spanish-language samples.
hypothesis: The gap in sharing between misinformation and true/neutral headlines is smaller among respondents in the top tertile of belief in disputed claims than in the bottom tertile (a positive infotype-by-moderator interaction). The penalty is present in both languages.
primary_outcome: Share: chosen/likely to share the headline (infotype x belief tertile interaction).
comparison: Misinformation vs true/neutral headline, interacted with belief tertile (top vs bottom), with respondent-clustered SEs; language is a secondary stratum.
unresolved: Actual headline images and Spanish translations must be supplied by the research team.
IRB number, compensation and panel vendor must be set by the research team.
label: Generalizability
